nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a nonempty finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $P = \operatorname{conv} s$ have dimension $d$. Then where $f_d = 1$ counts $P$ itself. Moving $f_d$ to the right gives the form in Ziegler's ICM report, and adding $f_{-1} = 1$ for the empty face gives $\sum_{k=-1}^{d} (-1)^k f_k = 0$. For $d = 3$ this is Euler's equation $f_0 - f_1 + f_2 = 2$, and for $d = 4$ it reads $f_0 - f_1 + f_2 - f_3 = 0$.
nodes.title: Euler–Poincaré relation

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a finite set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose convex hull $P$ has nonempty interior (so $P$ is a $d$-polytope) and is simplicial. Then there is a finite simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, in the sense of the Dehn–Sommerville page, with the same face numbers: $f_k(X) = f_k(P)$ for every $k < d$.
nodes.title: The boundary complex of a simplicial polytope is a simplicial sphere

nodes.summary: A triple $(f_0, f_1, f_2)$ of natural numbers is the f-vector of a 3-dimensional convex polytope (a finite point set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose convex hull has nonempty interior) if and only if So the f-vectors of 3-polytopes are exactly the integer points of a 2-dimensional polyhedral cone with apex $(4, 6, 4)$, the f-vector of the tetrahedron. The first condition is Euler's equation, the second is the upper bound…
nodes.title: Steinitz's lemma: the f-vectors of 3-polytopes

nodes.summary: Let $P = \operatorname{conv} s$ be a polytope of dimension $d$ with $m$ vertices. Then for every $k < d$, h_j(C_d(m)) = \binom{m-d-1+\min(j,d-j)}{\min(j, d-j)},$$ the number of $k$-dimensional faces of the cyclic polytope with $m$ vertices in dimension $d$. In Lean the right-hand side is the function `cyclicPolytopeFaceCount m d k` of the upper bound theorem for simplicial spheres, reused rather than redefined.
nodes.title: Upper bound theorem (McMullen)
